preamble: Prothetic [v] before word-initial back rounded vowels is a recurrent Slavic development. It gives a vowel-initial word a consonant onset. Belarusian and Ukrainian added v- before inherited initial *o and *u (Proto-Slavic *oko 'eye' > Belarusian вока, *uxo 'ear' > Ukrainian вухо). Russian has it in a few words such as восемь 'eight' from *osmь. Colloquial Common Czech adds v- to almost every word beginning with o- (Old Czech okno 'window' > vokno); Wikipedia dates the prothesis in the Bohemian dialects to the 14th century.

examples.note: Prothetic [v] before initial o; compare Russian око without prothesis.
Same prothesis before initial u; compare Russian ухо.
Prothetic v- before initial o, whose vowel later became i in the newly closed syllable.
Prothetic v- in a handful of Russian words.
Common Czech, the colloquial interdialect of Bohemia, adds v- to most words beginning with o-: votevřít vokno 'to open the window' (Wikipedia, Czech language).
Prothetic v- has been added to words beginning with o- in the Bohemian dialects since the 14th century, 'voko instead of oko' (Wikipedia, History of the Czech language).

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). History of the Czech language. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Czech_language
